Experience: Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in public works administration including facilities planning, capital program management, school construction, maintenance and operations, and transportation, including at least five (5) years in a senior management capacity with responsibility for budget administration, staff supervision, contract management, and major program leadership.

items.item_text: 01. Do you possess a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in construction management, architecture, engineering, facilities management, public administration, business administration, or a closely related field? If yes, please attach a copy of your degree upon submission of this application. Options: Yes | No
02. Do you have a valid California Class C driver's license? If yes, please attach a copy of your valid driver's license upon submission of this application. Options: Yes | No
Valid California Class C driver's license and maintain insurability under District vehicle insurance coverage.
Professional certification in Construction Management (CCM), Project Management (PMP), Facilities Management (CFM), or valid California Architectural/Engineering license is highly desirable.

Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in construction management, architecture, engineering, facilities management, public administration, business administration, or a closely related field. A Master's degree is highly desirable.

Experience: Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in public works administration including facilities planning, capital program management, school construction, maintenance and operations, and transportation, including at least five (5) years in a senior management capacity with responsibility for budget administration, staff supervision, contract management, and major program leadership.

Specialized Bond Experience: Demonstrated experience overseeing complex capital construction programs and voter-authorized general obligation bond programs, including direct responsibility for managing or evaluating external program management consultants, CBOC support, and bond audits is highly desirable.

Public Sector Context: Experience in a California K-12 school district or public agency involving DSA-regulated construction, OPSC state funding, California Public Contract Code, and Merit System labor relations is highly desirable.
Communicates District priorities, approval pathways, and decision timelines; verifies that consultants fulfill contracted scope and required service levels.

Critically reviews consultant deliverables; including master schedules, cost-to-complete forecasts, cash-flow projections, risk logs, payment applications, change orders, and closeout packages; requiring supporting documentation and risk analysis before forwarding recommendations to executive leadership.
Monitors consultant performance against contractual staffing commitments, metrics, and schedules; documents performance concerns and enforces corrective action plans within delegated authority.
Maintains District ownership and independent access to capital records, project control systems, financial data, and correspondence, ensuring institutional knowledge remains with the District.

Maintains operational readiness to assume direct day-to-day management of the bond program if contracted services expire, are terminated, or become unavailable. In such events, assumes direct leadership over project controls, consultants, contractors, and agency coordination until replacement management is established.

Plans, organizes, integrates, and evaluates District-wide FMOT and Bond Management programs; establishes service standards, performance measures, and departmental goals aligned with District strategic priorities.
Develops and recommends Board policies, administrative regulations, and operating standards governing facilities planning, construction, transportation, environmental safety, and public works.

Provides independent analysis, briefings, and recommendations to the Assistant Superintendent, Superintendent, Cabinet, and Governing Board; prepares and presents Board agenda items, financial reconciliations, and capital updates.
Represents the District with municipal, county, state, and federal agencies, utilities, legal counsel, community organizations, architects, engineers, and regulatory bodies.
Maintains alignment between voter-authorized bond language, Board-approved project lists, facilities master plans, and project budgets; identifies scope variances requiring executive or Board review.
Monitors and reconciles multi-year bond program budgets, commitments, encumbrances, cash flow, and cost-to-complete forecasts with District financial records in coordination with Fiscal Services.
Serves as primary staff liaison and resource to the Citizens' Bond Oversight Committee (CBOC); coordinates meeting materials, expenditure reports, and project status updates.
Coordinates support for independent financial and performance audits; validates documentation, prepares management responses, and implements audit recommendations.
Oversees project closeout workflows, Division of the State Architect (DSA) certification, financial retentions, warranties, and final acceptance recommendations.
Develops and maintains the District's Facilities Master Plan, integrating facility condition assessments, educational adequacy, demographic trends, and deferred maintenance strategies.
Evaluates project delivery methods, architectural plans, constructability reviews, bid specifications, and contract awards in consultation with Purchasing and legal counsel.
Evaluates proposed change orders, contractor claims, substitutions, and time extensions; negotiates terms and recommends approval within delegated limits.
Provides analysis regarding property acquisition, disposition, leases, joint-use agreements, developer fee mitigation, and CEQA/NEPA environmental compliance.

Provides general administrative direction to the Coordinator of Operations and Emergency Preparedness in leading custodial, maintenance, grounds, trades, and environmental health and safety programs; reviews higher-level operational standards.

Provides general administrative direction to the Coordinator of Transportation in leading home-to-school student transit, vehicle fleet management, and crossing guard programs; addresses escalated parental/safety complaints and major contract evaluations.
Develops and monitors annual operating budgets for FMOT functions; establishes internal expenditure approval controls and procurement workflows.
Selects, supervises, evaluates, and develops assigned management, supervisory, and classified personnel; establishes performance expectations and conducts performance evaluations.
Interprets collective bargaining agreements and Merit System rules; participates in grievance resolution, labor-management consultations, and workforce planning.
Ensures department compliance with Cal/OSHA, BAAQMD, hazardous materials requirements, fire codes, and ADA standards; oversees emergency response readiness.
Principles and practices of public sector management, strategic leadership, policy development, and Merit System administrative procedures.
General obligation bond program governance, Owner's Representative principles, CBOC reporting requirements, voter authorization compliance, and independent bond performance/financial audit defense.
Public school construction project management, including master scheduling, cost forecasting, contingency controls, change order analysis, constructability review, and DSA certification processes.
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations including California Education Code, Public Contract Code, CEQA/NEPA, DSA, OPSC, Cal/OSHA, BAAQMD, Title 13/Title 5, and ADA.
Principles and practices of facilities planning, maintenance operations, custodial standards, grounds management, environmental health and safety, and student transportation service delivery.
Public agency budgeting, fiscal controls, financial reconciliation between project control systems and general ledgers, contract negotiation, and procurement methods.
Principles of supervision, staff development, performance evaluation, labor relations, collective bargaining agreement administration, and grievance handling.
Lead, manage, and integrate District-wide FMOT functions and serve as primary internal Owner's Representative for voter-authorized bond and capital programs.
Direct and evaluate contracted bond program and project management consultants without duplicating contracted scope, while maintaining independent District controls and records.
Maintain operational readiness to assume direct day-to-day management of bond and capital projects if consultant services end or are reduced.
Provide administrative direction to subordinate management while delegating daily operational supervision, scheduling, and field dispatch.
Critically evaluate consultant recommendations, architectural plans, cost estimates, constructability reviews, change orders, and claims in the District's fiscal and operational interest.
Prepare clear, comprehensive, and objective executive briefings, Board agenda items, financial reconciliations, and CBOC reports.
Develop and administer multi-million-dollar capital budgets and departmental operating budgets.
Supervise, evaluate, and develop personnel; apply labor contracts and Merit System rules constructively.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing with executive leadership, Board members, public officials, regulatory agencies, staff, and community stakeholders.
Be flexible to perform work within changing priorities and possess sufficient interpersonal skills to work harmoniously with staff, students, administrators, parents, community members and others.
Travel in personal or District vehicle to school sites, construction locations, and public agency meetings.
